children.text: A marine theme park on the Manila Bay waterfront behind the Quirino Grandstand in Rizal Park. In half a day you can walk through an underwater tunnel with sharks and rays gliding overhead, visit the Humboldt penguin habitat and catch the sea lion and bird shows, which makes it an especially good fit for a Manila trip with children.
Manila Ocean Park is a marine theme park on the Manila Bay shore at the western end of Rizal Park, right behind the Quirino Grandstand stage. It opened on
March 1, 2008

and is run by the Philippine arm of a Singapore-linked company. It is far more than a single aquarium: the main aquarium building (the Oceanarium), a penguin habitat, an insect and amphibian gallery, sea lion and bird show arenas and a marine-themed hotel all share one complex, making it one of the easiest places in central Manila to spend half a day with kids.

The Oceanarium is the heart of the park. About 14,000 marine animals from around 277 species found in Philippine and Southeast Asian waters are displayed in seven zones holding some 3,000 m³ of seawater. In the middle of a walkway about
long is an acrylic underwater tunnel curved through 220 degrees, so you can stroll along while sharks, rays and big groupers swim over and beside you.
The complex has grown in recent years. The Ocean Park Aqua Adventure children's water park opened in
, the Philippine Biodome, a mostly open-air zoo under a transparent dome, opened in
late 2024

, and a digital media art gallery themed on flowers and light (the DNA Museum) followed. As a result, many visitors now buy online bundles that combine the basic Ocean Park ticket with the Biodome or the media art gallery.

Most exhibits are air-conditioned and indoors, so the park works on scorching afternoons and rainy days alike, and children 2 feet (about 61cm) tall or under get in free, which makes it popular with families with young kids, including Korean families living in the Philippines. That said, the facility has been open for a long time and reviews regularly mention cloudy or worn tanks, so rather than expecting a world-class mega-aquarium, think of it as a light outing to pair with Rizal Park and Manila Bay.

The highlight of a route that starts in a freshwater jungle zone and continues through coral reef and deep-sea zones. Sharks and rays pass overhead in the 220-degree curved tunnel; go right after opening, when it is quiet, and you can take photos in the tunnel at your own pace.

The first penguin facility in the Philippines, where you see Humboldt penguins from the coasts of South America up close through the glass. It comes with an Antarctic-themed walkway and a Christmas Village, and penguin feeding with a photo is a separate paid experience limited to 100 sessions a day.

blocks.title: Sea lion show and All Star Bird Show

children.text: Back-to-back shows feature South American sea lions followed by parrots, cockatoos and birds of prey. They run at
and
on weekdays, with an extra
show on weekends and public holidays, and each session takes about
45 minutes

The Stingray Dry Encounter, where you put your hand into a shallow pool to touch rays, is included in the standard package. Staff show you how to touch them, so just hold your child's hand and follow their directions.

A gallery of small creatures such as spiders, insects, worms and poison dart frogs. Keepers also hold show-and-tell sessions where they bring animals out and talk about them, so bug-loving kids tend to linger here.

A zoo set under a transparent dome next to Ocean Park. Highlights are the crocodile tunnel, where you pass a saltwater crocodile about 14 feet (about 4.3m) long through a glass tube, plus otters, seals and hornbills, and there are animal talks three times a day. A separate ticket or bundle is required.

The DNA Museum is an immersive digital art gallery built around flowers, light and sound and is great for photos, while Aqua Adventure is a children's water park with slides and a water-gun playground. Both need separate tickets, and you will need swimwear for the water park.
Arrive at opening time, show your online voucher QR code and go in. On weekends and public holidays the park opens at 9 AM.
Visit the Oceanarium. Start with the underwater tunnel while crowds are thin and take your time.
Try the stingray encounter and explore World of Creepy Crawlies.
Have an early lunch at a restaurant or snack stand inside the complex. Outside food is not allowed.
Watch the sea lion show and the All Star Bird Show back to back. Arrive about 10 minutes early for front-row seats.
See the Trails to Antarctica penguin habitat and sign up for penguin feeding if you like.
Browse the souvenir shop and leave. You cannot re-enter an exhibit once you exit, so make sure you have not missed anything.
If you bought a bundle, head next door to the Philippine Biodome or the DNA Museum.
Catch the Biodome's afternoon animal talk and walk through the crocodile tunnel.
Leave the complex and walk through Rizal Park past the front of the Quirino Grandstand.
Head to the Manila Bay waterfront promenade along Roxas Boulevard to watch the sunset.
Finish with dinner at a restaurant in Ermita or Malate, or at Robinsons Place Manila.
Last entry at the Biodome and the DNA Museum is also around
5 PM
, so if you want to see both, it is best to finish Ocean Park in the morning.
The park is about
10km
from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL). A Grab ride takes
30 minutes–1 hour 20 minutes
depending on traffic and costs about
. Enter "Manila Ocean Park" as the destination and you will be dropped at the complex entrance.
After the
fare increase, the flag-down rate for yellow airport taxis is
(first 500m). Always make sure the meter is on.
Get off at United Nations Avenue station on LRT Line 1, cross Roxas Boulevard and walk west through Rizal Park for
15–20 minutes
. The fare is about
depending on your starting station.
From Makati, take MRT-3 to Taft Avenue station and transfer to LRT-1 EDSA station; from the Quezon City side, take LRT-2 to Recto station and walk over to LRT-1 Doroteo Jose station.
From Makati, Grab takes
30 minutes–1 hour
and costs about
, more at rush hour and on rainy days. For families with kids and lots of bags, this is the easiest option.
From the hotel area in Ermita and Malate it is a
10–15 minute
drive. On the way back, use the taxi stand or the Grab pickup point near the main gate.

Coming from the south (Pasay and Makati), turn left from Roxas Boulevard onto T.M. Kalaw Street near the US Embassy; from the north, enter via Katigbak Drive or T.M. Kalaw Street. Entering the destination into a map app is the most reliable way.
There are two parking areas, the South Parking near Harbor View and the North Parking near the Manila Hotel. Cars pay
for the first
3 hours
and
for each additional hour.
Take a jeepney marked "Luneta" along Roxas Boulevard or Taft Avenue, get off at Rizal Park and walk. From
September 28, 2026
the minimum fare is
for traditional jeepneys and
for modern jeepneys. First-time visitors will find Grab or the LRT much easier.
The Oceanarium, penguin habitat and insect gallery are indoors, so you can visit year-round. Manila's dry season runs from
December–May
, and
December–February
is relatively cool, making it pleasant to stroll Rizal Park and Manila Bay after the park. In
March–May
daytime temperatures often top
, so walking between the partly roofed amphitheater and the other buildings gets hot.
In the rainy season from
June–November

, afternoon showers are frequent, and when a typhoon passes, the coastal stretch of Roxas Boulevard can flood. The park may close temporarily under a strong typhoon warning, so check its official Facebook page before you go. The day of the week matters more than the season: weekends, public holidays, the summer school break (April–May) and the year-end holidays bring crowds of families, filling the show seats and restaurants. For a relaxed visit, go on a weekday, ideally right after opening.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions. Online bundles change name and contents every two or three months, so check which attractions are included on the official website before buying.

Hotel H2O, a marine-themed hotel, is attached to the complex. Some rooms have an aquarium for one wall, so you can watch fish from your bed, and rooms facing Manila Bay look out over the sunset, so many families stay a night with their kids. Room rates are around
a night depending on the date and room type. For more choice, Ermita and Malate across Rizal Park have plenty of mid-range hotels at about
a night. The Manila Hotel, a long-established luxury hotel on the north side of Rizal Park, is also within walking distance.

Outside food and drinks are not allowed in Ocean Park, so you will eat lunch inside the complex. There is Makan Makan, an Asian food court, a garden café and several stands selling burgers, adobo and desserts, at about
per person per meal. After your visit, try Filipino dishes such as sinigang, adobo and halo-halo at the restaurants in Robinsons Place Manila mall or at Filipino restaurants in Malate.
Always buy your tickets online in advance. The official website bundle costs about
, less than half the walk-in regular price, but it can only be used from the day after purchase, so buy it by the day before.
Opening hours are
10 AM–6 PM
on weekdays and
9 AM–6 PM
on weekends and public holidays, and last entry to the Oceanarium is
. Details differ slightly between information pages, so check before you go.
Check the day's show schedule as soon as you enter and plan your route around the show times to cut down on waiting.
Children 2 feet (about 61cm) tall or under are free; anyone taller needs a ticket regardless of age. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult.
The penguin habitat is kept cool, so bring a light jacket. If you plan to visit the water park too, pack swimwear and a change of clothes.
Wheelchairs can be borrowed free of charge by leaving an ID, and getting around with a stroller is easy enough.
Senior and PWD discounts apply only to the regular price and cannot be combined with online discounts. Pick whichever is cheaper.
For families, following a half-day visit with Rizal Park and a Manila Bay sunset rounds out a full day naturally.

Each attraction allows only one entry. Once you leave the Oceanarium or the penguin habitat, you cannot go back in on the same ticket, so take care of restroom breaks and meals first. Ticket bundles and show times change often, so check the latest notices.
Outside food and drinks are caught at the bag check at the entrance, so finish snacks and drinks before you go in.
To protect the animals, flash photography, tapping on the glass and feeding are prohibited, and drones, professional camera gear and pets are not allowed.
Buy tickets only from the official website or authorized booking apps. Cheap tickets on social media may be fake or unusable.
Park rules state that people with respiratory conditions or asthma may be refused entry, so ask in advance if this applies to you.
When walking through Rizal Park, watch out for pickpockets and self-styled guides who ask for money, and use Grab after dark.
Right in front of the park; from the Quirino Grandstand it is about a
10-minute
walk to the Rizal Monument. A city park honoring the Philippines' national hero.
A
5–10 minute
walk from the shore beside the complex to the Roxas Boulevard promenade, where you can see Manila's most famous sunset.
About a
20-minute
walk to the eastern end of Rizal Park. Its three museums of fine arts, anthropology and natural history are free and air-conditioned, which makes them good with kids.
